thread:
alex: Prod alert — throughput down ~40% for redwood-xl-1 in us-west starting 2024-07-09 10:31 UTC. Multiple worker restarts and OOMs. I opened this thread.

ops-bot: Alert: worker_restarts>5 in 5m on pool gpu-highmem-1. OOM events: 12. Page-fragmentation metric elevated. Grafana: <https://grafana/redwood/d/abcd123/throughput>

maria: I'm on it :eyes: Pulling recent perf traces and kv metrics.

jing: Seeing kvcache_evictions spike at 10:30: evict_rate=11873/s. KV cache occupancy dropped ~68% across nodes. Also a surge of long-seq (>2k tokens) single-request workloads.

devon: Ran quick `nvidia-smi` on one affected node (gpu-24) — memory looks split across many small allocations, not dominated by 1 big process. Paste:
```
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Processes:                                                       GPU Memory |
|  GPU   PID   Type   Process name                                Usage      |
|    0  14233  C      python redwood_server                        7199MiB    |
|    0  14289  C      python batch_worker                          6201MiB    |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

nate: Runtime logs show kernel-selection falling back to matmul_generic around the spike. Example: 
```
[10:30:41] kernel_selector: chosen=matmul_generic reason=\"no_optimized_kern_for_seqlen\"
[10:30:41] allocator: alloc_retry, trying slab_sweep
[10:30:41] kvcache: evict key 0x7ff4...\n```

alex: Hypothesis: regression in kernel-selection heuristic caused many requests to pick slower/unoptimized kernels -> higher transient allocations + KV eviction storms -> fragmentation -> OOM -> worker restarts. Also, batch sampler allowed big single-request batches to mix with many small ones increasing max_seq_in_batch and peak allocation.

maria: I reproduced locally with a mixed workload: 1 long request (3k tokens) interleaved with many short (32 token) requests triggers fallback + eviction loop. Repro is solid.

jing: Quick mitigation plan: rollback kernel-selection change from yesterday (rev r12c -> r12b) to canary pool; clamp batch max_tokens to 1024 for gpu-highmem pools; disable batching for long-seq requests via sampler rule.

devon: Deployed rollback to canary at 10:48 UTC. Also pushed KV tuning: increase slab_compaction_frequency to 10s and lower default_kv_capacity to reduce eviction churn.

ops-bot: Mitigations applied: rollback=r12b -> canary; batch_max_tokens=1024 applied to gpu-highmem-1; kv.slab_compaction_freq=10s. Incident ticket updated.

nate: Post-rollback traces show kernel_selector choosing fused_qkv for long-seq again. OOMs dropped to zero and worker restarts stopped within ~4m of rollout. p95 latency recovered gradually.

alex: Root cause (working hypothesis): kernel-selection regression in r12c mis-classified some long-seq layouts as incompatible with optimized kernels; combined with recent traffic spike of long-context requests and mixed batch packing, which increased peak temporary allocations. KV cache eviction heuristic amplified fragmentation and caused cascading OOMs.

maria: Action items (owners):
- revert kernel-selection regression permanently (jing)
- add unit/integration tests for kernel selection with mixed seqlen workloads (nate)
- protective sampler rule to clamp max_tokens for mixed batches + feature flag (devon)
- add alert: kv_eviction_rate > 5k/s for >1m (alex)
- postmortem writeup + customer-facing note for impacted tenants (maria)

devon: Timeline: first OOM 10:31, rollback to canary 10:48, OOMs ceased ~10:52, throughput restored by ~10:56.

alex: Thanks everyone. I'll start the postmortem doc and link it here once drafted.

sentry-bot: New issue created: INC-2024-1136 - Kernel-selection regression causing OOM/throughput drop. Priority: P2.

maria: quick follow-up — adding a perf test harness for mixed seqlen sampling to CI tomorrow. :thumbsup:
